profile.entities: Aeroflex Industries Ltd (parent); Hyd-Air Engineering (subsidiary); undisclosed US multinational liquid-cooling partner (5-yr India-exclusive supply)
profile.mgmt: Mr. Asad Daud — Managing Director; Strategic Growth Advisors (IR)
profile.subseg: SS hoses & hose-assemblies; metal bellows; miniature metal bellows; liquid-cooling skid assemblies (data centers); Hyd-Air (CNC hydraulic components)
profile.themes: Data-center / AI-infrastructure liquid cooling (high); Renewable/EV — adjacent optionality only (flow-control adaptable to EV/semiconductor cooling)

bull_bear.body:
- No debt; does not plan to raise debt. Preferential allotment in-principle approval received; funds expected imminently.
- Cash ~INR 20 cr (as of 31-Dec-2025).
- Disciplined: cut low-visibility miniature-bellows outlay, redeploy to demand-backed projects (liquid cooling, hoses, annealing).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- US tariff (50%) — biggest market (US ~55% of exports); blocks new-customer onboarding; bellows ramp delayed.
- Heavy export concentration (74% sales; EU+US ~85% of exports) and single-customer dependence in liquid cooling (5-yr exclusive, India-only).
- Liquid-cooling demand entirely partner-forecast-driven; data-center capex cyclicality.
- Execution: capacity additions across hoses/assemblies/bellows running behind schedule.
- SS raw-material price volatility (partially hedged).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident but measured ("Q3 good, not very good"); candid on Q1 weakness, bellows being behind schedule, and tariff drag on new customers. Emphasis on long-term margin path and moat narrative.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Liquid-cooling skid is flow-control IP adaptable beyond data centers (large machinery, semiconductor, HVAC, EV cooling) — collapse-of-DC optionality.
- Partner intends to make the India entity a **global supply hub** for skid assemblies in 3–4 years (exports possible ~6 months out) — large latent upside beyond the India-only INR 350 cr peak.
- Moat = 15–20 yrs flow-control engineering + proprietary flow-simulation software + customer access, not just "changing a hose design."
- Assembly growth is self-reinforcing: more assemblies → more captive hose-braid production.
- India–EU FTA structurally neutralizes Turkish duty-free advantage in EU.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

business.body:
- **Hoses & assemblies** — core; assemblies (hose+braid) the growth focus, mgmt wants share to keep rising. Capacity +1M meters added this month → 17.5M; → 20M phased by Q2FY27.
- **Metal bellows** — run-rate INR 12 cr; Phase-2 (120k→300k units) deferred until Phase-1 optimal.
- **Miniature metal bellows** — capex cut INR 23 cr → INR 10.5 cr; capacity 240k → ~50–60k units/yr; peak only ~INR 8–9 cr; demand slower than hoped.
- **Liquid cooling (skid assemblies)** — first commercial dispatch done; capacity 2,000 → 15,000 units/yr by Jun-2026; new Chakan (Pune) support plant; capex <INR 100 cr; ~INR 3 lakh/piece realization at 80% utilization. Margins better than hoses, in line with assemblies.
- **Hyd-Air (subsidiary)** — revenue INR 8.5 cr (vs INR 2.9 cr YoY); ~70% utilization; capex planned.
business.title: Segment

business.body:
| Challenge | Direction | Name | Role | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Data-center / AI liquid-cooling ramp | beneficiary | Aeroflex Industries (AEROFLEX) | Skid-assembly maker, India-exclusive partner | High | New high-margin leg, partner global-hub intent |
| India–EU FTA (vs Turkey duty-free) | beneficiary | Aeroflex Industries (AEROFLEX) | SS hose/assembly exporter to EU | Med | EU was flat ~3 yrs; FTA tailwind |
| 50% US tariff | loser | Aeroflex Industries (AEROFLEX) | Exporter, US ~55% of exports | Med | New-customer onboarding stalled; 8% price hit |
| Shift air→liquid cooling in new DCs | beneficiary | Undisclosed US liquid-cooling MNC partner | Tech/design owner, demand-forecast provider | Med | (code unverified) — counterparty, not listed proxy named |
| Domestic infra (ports/terminals, steel) demand | beneficiary | Aeroflex Industries (AEROFLEX) | Flow-component supplier | Med | New ports/chemical customers won |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as a leading manufacturer of metallic flexible flow solutions with 28 years of industry leadership, 3,300+ SKUs, exports to 90+ countries and a customised-solution model for high-end applications.
- Claims high entry barriers built on engineering-intensive products, strong technical expertise, in-house R&D/customisation and long-standing customer relationships.
- Frames itself as an approved supplier to a leading global provider of digital infrastructure and thermal management solutions, giving access to global and domestic data centre deployments.
- Sells into both traditional sectors (oil & gas, steel, petrochemicals, chemicals/pharma, paper) and emerging ones (data centres, semiconductors, hydrogen, solar, electric mobility, robotics, aerospace & defence).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Governance] Board oversight includes independent directors drawn from the Tata Group, Ashok Leyland and Senior India, with the company under professional management.
- [Digital] Building a connected digital backbone with integrated SAP ERP across finance, inventory and production planning (production lines linked via tablets for real-time machine efficiency) and Salesforce CRM covering lead-to-fulfilment.
- [Ownership] Established in 1998 and acquired in 2018 by Aeroflex Enterprises Limited (formerly Sat Industries Limited).
- [Market] Cites a global liquid cooling market CAGR of 33.2% and direct-to-chip cooling CAGR of 35.0% over CY25-CY32e, plus a 9+ GW announced Indian data centre pipeline over five years led by Reliance Jio, Adani, TCS, CapitaLand, Nxtra, STT GDC India, CtrlS and Yotta.
- [Recognition] Great Place to Work certification 2025-26, 16th CII National HR Excellence Award 2025-26 and EEPC India Export Excellence Awards (Western Region) for 2022-23 and 2023-24; participated in Data Center World Exhibition, USA in April 2026.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- Q3 EBITDA margin 23.5–23.6%, mix-led (value-added 54%). Took 8% price discount on US tariff but protected bottom line via internal cost optimization + vendor cost-sharing.
- Liquid-cooling margins undisclosed (single-customer confidentiality) but > hoses, ~= assemblies.
- RM (SS wire/coil) managed via back-to-back planning + long-term supplier contracts; prices broadly stable last couple of years.
latest_quarter.title: Margins

latest_quarter.body:
- New: First commercial dispatch of liquid-cooling flow-control components & skid assemblies; skid capacity expansion to 15,000 units (by Jun-26); new Chakan (Pune) support plant.
- New: India–EU FTA announced — flagged as near-term EU growth booster.
- Cut: Miniature metal bellows capex INR 23 cr → INR 10.5 cr; capacity 240k → ~50–60k units/yr (vs prior 240k plan); metal-bellows Phase-2 (120k→300k) deferred.
- Disclosure gap vs prior quarters: end-user industry mix not provided this quarter (analyst flagged); skid margins withheld (single-customer confidentiality).
- Capacity: +1M meters hose added this month → 17.5M; balance 2.5M phased to Q2FY27.
- Subsidiary: Hyd-Air revenue jumped to INR 8.5 cr (from INR 2.9 cr YoY); capex expansion to be announced.
- Mix: Value-added products now 54% of 9M sales (vs ~52% assemblies traction noted by analyst).
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- EBITDA margin target 23–25% over next couple of years (vs ~20–21% two years ago); aspiration to ~25%.
- If 50% US tariff is resolved, margins materially higher (mgmt would not quantify; an analyst floated +400–500bps).
- Hose+assembly capacity reaches 20M meters; balance 2.5M meters phased to Q2FY27. Peak hose+assembly revenue INR 650–675 cr (assuming ~70% from assemblies).
- Liquid-cooling peak revenue INR 300–350 cr, peak utilization ~FY29 (2–2.5 yrs); near-term dispatch pipeline INR 45 cr.
- Metal bellows: current run-rate INR 12 cr → INR 36 cr in next few quarters; peak ~INR 85 cr by end-FY28/start-FY29 (behind schedule due to US tariff delays).
- Hyd-Air: INR 45 cr peak at current capacity (capex to expand coming soon).
- Aggregate peak revenue potential >INR 1,000 cr over next ~3 years.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- Liquid-cooling skid pipeline INR 45 cr scheduled for dispatch per partner's plan (India-only currently).
- US: no order cancellations; repeat orders from existing customers resuming; new-customer/OEM onboarding delayed by tariffs.
- Domestic order traction in steel, ports & terminals, chemicals; Hyd-Air strong in railways.
outlook.title: Order book

outlook.body:
- Quarterly exports +30% YoY (EU major contributor) despite tariffs; 9M export growth still single-digit due to very weak Q1.
- EU framed as next strong leg — India–EU FTA expected to boost competitiveness vs Turkey (duty-free EU access); EU was flat ~3 years.
- Domestic up strongly 9M — new ports/terminals & chemical customers, deeper wallet share in steel.
- Liquid-cooling TAM: global ~$3bn now, ~33% CAGR → ~$21bn over 6–7 yrs.
outlook.title: Growth

deepdive.thesis: Niche, cash-generative SS flexible-flow maker pivoting up the value chain — value-added products (assemblies/fittings/bellows/skids) now 54% of 9M sales — with a new, high-optionality leg in data-center liquid-cooling skid assemblies under a 5-year India-exclusive deal with a US multinational. Highest-ever quarterly revenue/EBITDA/PAT despite a 50% US tariff and an 8% price discount, offset by internal cost engineering and supply-chain sharing.
